name: Invention of Writing
description: Cuneiform emerges in Sumer from accounting tokens, and hieroglyphs appear in Egypt at nearly the same moment — the threshold of recorded history, making law, literature, contracts, and administration durable beyond living memory.

name: Bronze Age Collapse
description: Within decades, nearly every major eastern-Mediterranean civilization — Mycenaean Greece, the Hittite Empire, Ugarit — fell amid raids by the 'Sea Peoples', drought, earthquakes, and systems failure. Writing vanished in Greece for four centuries.

name: Battle of Marathon
description: Outnumbered Athenian hoplites routed the first Persian invasion of Greece on the plain of Marathon, preserving the young Athenian democracy and entering legend via the runner Pheidippides.

name: Founding of the Roman Republic
description: Rome expelled its last king, Tarquin the Proud, and vested power in elected consuls, a senate, and assemblies — the constitutional experiment whose offices, checks, and vocabulary still underlie western government.

name: Crossing of the Rubicon
description: Julius Caesar led a legion across the small river bounding his province — an act of treason that started the civil war ending the Roman Republic, and an enduring idiom for the irreversible step.

name: Fall of the Western Roman Empire
description: The Germanic general Odoacer deposed the boy-emperor Romulus Augustulus and sent the imperial regalia to Constantinople — the conventional endpoint of the western empire after a century of fiscal crisis, migration, and fragmentation.

name: The Hijra
description: Muhammad's migration from Mecca to Medina, where the first Muslim polity formed — year one of the Islamic calendar. Within a century the caliphate stretched from Iberia to the Indus.

name: Coronation of Charlemagne
description: Pope Leo III crowned the Frankish king Emperor of the Romans in St Peter's on Christmas Day — reviving the western imperial title, binding papacy and empire in mutual dependence, and defining the medieval order.

name: Norman Conquest of England
description: William of Normandy's victory at Hastings replaced England's ruling class, transformed English law, land-holding, and language (injecting thousands of French words), and reoriented the kingdom toward France for four centuries.

name: Magna Carta
description: Rebel barons forced King John to seal a charter conceding that the crown was subject to law — including protection from arbitrary imprisonment. Repeatedly reissued, it became the touchstone of constitutional liberty.

name: The Black Death
description: Yersinia pestis, carried along trade routes from Central Asia, killed perhaps a third to half of Europe's population and tens of millions across Eurasia and North Africa — shattering labour systems, hastening serfdom's decline in the West, and scarring culture for generations.

name: Fall of Constantinople
description: Mehmed II's cannon breached the Theodosian Walls, ending the thousand-year Byzantine Empire. Greek scholars and manuscripts flowing west fed the Renaissance; the Ottomans gained an imperial capital astride Europe and Asia.

name: Columbian Contact
description: Columbus's landfall in the Caribbean began permanent exchange between hemispheres: American crops (potato, maize) transformed Old World diets while Eurasian diseases killed the great majority of indigenous Americans, and colonization and the Atlantic slave trade followed.

name: Posting of the Ninety-five Theses
description: Martin Luther's challenge to indulgences, amplified by the printing press, escalated into the Protestant Reformation — splitting western Christianity and igniting a century of religious war and state formation.

name: Peace of Westphalia
description: The treaties ending the Thirty Years' War normalized religious coexistence within the Empire and became shorthand for the modern principle of sovereign territorial states as the units of international order.

name: American Declaration of Independence
description: Thirteen colonies declared separation from Britain, grounding legitimacy in natural rights and consent of the governed — a template invoked by independence movements ever since.

name: Storming of the Bastille
description: A Paris crowd seized the royal fortress-prison, symbol of arbitrary power, tipping the fiscal crisis of the French monarchy into full revolution — the Declaration of the Rights of Man followed within weeks.

name: British Abolition of the Slave Trade
description: After decades of campaigning by abolitionists and resistance by the enslaved, Parliament outlawed the Atlantic slave trade; the Royal Navy's West Africa Squadron then policed it. Slavery itself in British colonies was abolished in 1833.

name: Publication of the Communist Manifesto
description: Marx and Engels's pamphlet, appearing as revolutions swept Europe, distilled class struggle into a program that would organize labour movements and, in the twentieth century, states governing a third of humanity.

name: Assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand
description: Gavrilo Princip's shots in Sarajevo triggered the alliance cascade that became the First World War — four years, four fallen empires, and some seventeen million dead.

name: October Revolution
description: Lenin's Bolsheviks seized Petrograd from the Provisional Government, pulling Russia from the war and founding the world's first communist state — the defining geopolitical fact of the twentieth century.

name: Atomic Bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki
description: American B-29s destroyed two Japanese cities with the first nuclear weapons used in war, killing well over one hundred thousand people. Japan surrendered days later; the nuclear age's deterrence politics began.

name: Indian Independence and Partition
description: British India became independent India and Pakistan at midnight on 15 August 1947. Partition uprooted some fifteen million people along religious lines and killed hundreds of thousands to two million in communal violence.

name: Apollo 11 Moon Landing
description: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin walked on the Moon while Michael Collins orbited above — the culmination of the space race watched by a fifth of humanity, and still the farthest humans have travelled.

name: Fall of the Berlin Wall
description: After a botched press conference, East Berliners surged through the checkpoints and the Wall was breached amid celebration — the emblematic end of the Cold War division of Europe; Germany reunified within a year.

name: Invention of the World Wide Web
description: At CERN, Tim Berners-Lee combined hypertext with the internet — HTTP, HTML, URLs, and the first browser — and released it royalty-free, creating the platform that reorganized commerce, media, and social life.
